title: Public facing privacy policy is inaccurate, omits critical information, and/or is out of date.
description:

Breach of transparency obligations

title: Databases - Sensitive data stored in plain text
Company records are altered due to lack of proper access controls, segregation of duties, and/or supervision.
description: All data stored on production databases are available only for the head of engineering and the CEO.

title: Entrances - Physical security: No offices
Personnel fraudulently pay "ghost employees" due to lack of segregation, approvals and/or oversight in the payroll process.
description: Payment process is conducted by Operations Manager, Heads of Departments and validated by the controller before any payment is released.
treatmentPlan: The head of each department has the responsability to maintain a current headcount of their department, Operation Manager consolidates and prepare the payments and the controller review and approves. Based on our current scenario three reviewers interact with the payment process.

title: Authentication mechanisms - Your codebase: codebase exposed
description:
1- Implemented role-based access control (RBAC) and multi-factor authentication (MFA) for your code repositories.
2- Regular code reviews to check for any sensitive data or hardcoded credentials in the codebase.
3- We have set up monitoring tools to detect any unusual access or changes to the codebase.

title: Codebase security - Your codebase: Access compromised
description:
1- Implement role-based access controls (RBAC) and require multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users accessing the codebase.
2- We have set up audit logs to track who accesses or modifies the codebase and when these changes occur.
3- Periodically review user access rights to ensure that only authorized personnel have access to sensitive code.

title: The company assists employees in purchasing laptops for work purposes, but these devices are not returned upon offboarding, and there is no formal device disposal policy. This introduces risks related to data leakage, unauthorized access to corporate resources, or failure to comply with data protection regulations, as these devices may not be securely wiped or destroyed when employees leave the organization.
treatmentPlan:
1. Implementing a Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policy with clear guidelines.
2. Adding encryption and multi-factor authentication (MFA) requirements for remote access.
3. security awareness training for employees using personal devices.
4. Mandate that employees agree to certain security controls (e.g., encryption, anti-virus, device management, etc.) before using personal devices for work.
5. Update the offboarding process to include a mandatory security checklist for any devices the employee retains, ensuring that company data is securely wiped or transferred.
